content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Oxnard

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Review PMI's eligibility criteria—typically a secondary degree plus years of project leadership experience, or a bachelor's degree with fewer years required. Verify your background meets the standard before enrolling.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. Attend all sessions synchronously from Oxnard or anywhere with internet access. This formal education fulfills PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement and covers the PMBOK® Guide framework, exam domains, and real-world scenarios.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After course completion, create your PMI account and submit your PMP application directly to PMI. Document your project experience, education, and references as requested. Pay the exam fee and wait for PMI to audit and approve your application before scheduling your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Pass the PMP Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, practice questions, and study guides to reinforce course material. Schedule your exam at a PMI-approved testing center. Sit for the computer-based PMP exam, which assesses your knowledge across the five process groups and ten knowledge areas.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, maintain your PMP by earning professional development units (PDUs) throughout a three-year renewal cycle. Engage in approved learning activities—training, volunteering, teaching, or publications—and renew your credential before expiration to keep it active and current.
